ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Jesse Owens

text.paragraph: Subsequent annual wellness visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Owens, now 66, returns for his subsequent annual wellness visit three weeks after his post-operative review; his last wellness visit was at his previous clinic a year ago. He is nine weeks past a thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy, after three cycles of chemoimmunotherapy, and has had no further cancer treatment since. He goes to pulmonary rehabilitation twice a week and walks 2.5 km most mornings. He has not smoked for four and a half months and takes varenicline 1 mg twice daily without side effects. He has gone back to speaking at two schools. He completed the health risk assessment beforehand and asked to talk about what he would want if the cancer came back. [S]

Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting screening finding in a long-term smoker. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration
S — Synthetic histology, stage and biomarkers linked to his documented adenocarcinoma of the left lung; in the modern episode it is found by screening while still resectable.
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: a pack a day for 35 years (35 pack-years); smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking; two attempts to stop, each lasting a few weeks without medicine
S — Synthetic modern entry linked to his documented smoking; superseded at the visit after surgery by nicotine dependence in early remission.

S — Synthetic intercurrent illness; not a historical claim.

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 25 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and completed an Arizona health care power of attorney. He wants every treatment that offers a real chance of controlling the cancer if it comes back, including more surgery, radiation or medicines. If the cancer returned and could no longer be controlled, he would want his symptoms treated well and to stay at home, with his family and his church, rather than spend his last weeks in intensive care, and he would not want resuscitation in that situation. He wants his story told to young people so that they never start smoking. To be revisited at any change in his health and at least yearly. [S]
